messages:
olivia: Quick sanity check — adding a KMS grant + IRSA role for the secretstore sidecar in staging. Can someone do a quick pre-merge skim? TL;DR and snippets below.

henry: pinging infra for a quick review, thx. please paste the tf snippet if you have it.

olivia: here is what I have so far:
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_grant" "secretstore_irsa" {
  name               = "secretstore-irsa-grant"
  key_id             = aws_kms_key.secrets.id
  grantee_principal  = "arn:aws:iam::${data.aws_caller_identity.current.account_id}:role/eks-irsa-secretstore"
  operations         = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  constraints {
    encryption_context_subset = {
      "k8s.io/serviceaccount/namespace" = "staging"
      "k8s.io/serviceaccount/name"      = "secretstore-sa"
    }
  }
}
```

olivia: and the kube manifest has the SA annotation:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: secretstore-sa
  namespace: staging
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::<acct-id>:role/eks-irsa-secretstore
```

priya: Two quick notes: 1) The aws_kms_grant grantee_principal can be a role ARN, that part looks fine. 2) Make sure the encryption context keys you use match exactly what the sidecar sets — case matters.

dmitri: Are you creating the IAM role with an AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity policy (IRSA)? If you plan to use session tags/conditions, ensure your key policy allows those tag-based conditions (e.g., aws:PrincipalTag/eks.amazonaws.com/serviceaccount/name).

olivia: yes role created from module: 
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "irsa_secretstore" {
  name               = "eks-irsa-secretstore"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}
```

henry: also check ordering — KMS key/key policy must allow CreateGrant for whoever is creating the grant. We usually include a key policy that allows the account principal to call kms:CreateGrant, otherwise tf apply fails.

infra-bot: Reminder: run `tf plan -target=aws_kms_grant.secretstore_irsa` if you want to preview just the grant changes.

priya: :thumbsup: one more nit: encryption_context_subset is great but verify the sidecar actually sends both keys (namespace + name). If one missing, the grant condition won't match.

olivia: good call — I'll add the key policy snippet and a short smoke test for the sidecar to assert the encryption context. planning to land in a canary ns first.

dmitri: optional: add a lifecycle ignore_changes on the grant id during the initial rollout to avoid drift noise if the provider recreates it. saved us in the past.

henry: LGTM after those small tweaks.

olivia: thanks all — will update the PR and ping when ready for final.
